ELECTRICITY — MOCK EXAM #14
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: ELECTRICITY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Speaker
   B. CPU
   C. Keyboard
   D. Monitor

2. When learning Measuring Instruments, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Measuring Instruments.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Measuring Instruments.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Measuring Instruments.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Measuring Instruments.

3. When learning Earthing and Excess Current Protection, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Earthing and Excess Current Protection.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Earthing and Excess Current Protection.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Earthing and Excess Current Protection.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Earthing and Excess Current Protection.

4. When learning Power Supplies, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Power Supplies.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Power Supplies.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Power Supplies.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Power Supplies.

5. When learning Electrical Diagrams, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Electrical Diagrams.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Electrical Diagrams.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Electrical Diagrams.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Electrical Diagrams.

6. When learning Electronics 4.4 Project Identification, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Electronics 4.4 Project Identification.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Electronics 4.4 Project Identification.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Electronics 4.4 Project Identification.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Electronics 4.4 Project Identification.

7. When learning Wiring Systems and Regulations, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Wiring Systems and Regulations.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Wiring Systems and Regulations.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Wiring Systems and Regulations.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Wiring Systems and Regulations.

8. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Information and Communication Technology
   B. Internal Cooking Timer
   C. Input Cable Tester
   D. International Cricket Team

9. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   B. Overload every socket
   C. Ignore burnt cables
   D. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun

10. When learning DC Generators, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for DC Generators.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after DC Generators.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for DC Generators.
   D. Skip safety briefings for DC Generators.

11. When learning Single Phase AC Generators, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Single Phase AC Generators.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Single Phase AC Generators.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Single Phase AC Generators.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Single Phase AC Generators.

12. When learning Orthographic Projection, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Orthographic Projection.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Orthographic Projection.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Orthographic Projection.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Orthographic Projection.

13. When learning Single Stage Bipolar Junction Transistor Amplifier, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Single Stage Bipolar Junction Transistor Amplifier.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Single Stage Bipolar Junction Transistor Amplifier.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Single Stage Bipolar Junction Transistor Amplifier.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Single Stage Bipolar Junction Transistor Amplifier.

14. When learning Inspection and Testing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Inspection and Testing.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Inspection and Testing.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Inspection and Testing.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Inspection and Testing.

15. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Work alone with eyes closed
   B. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   C. Run with the tool
   D. Remove all guards

16. When learning Single Phase AC Circuits, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Single Phase AC Circuits.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Single Phase AC Circuits.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Single Phase AC Circuits.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Single Phase AC Circuits.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain DC Generators and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Single Phase AC Generators and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Wiring Systems and Regulations and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Single Stage Bipolar Junction Transistor Amplifier and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Electronics 4.4 Project Identification and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
